framework.name: CSTA K-12 Computer Science Standards
framework.source: https://csteachers.org/k12standards (five concepts; wording is the school's own)

objectives.description: Describe the parts of a computer, including hardware, software and the operating system, and how they work together.
Troubleshoot a simple computing problem using a systematic approach.
Write a program in a block or text language that uses sequence, variables and output.
Use conditionals to make a program respond to different inputs.
Use loops to repeat actions and simplify a program.
Break a problem into smaller parts and write a procedure for each.
Design an algorithm in pseudocode or a flowchart before coding it.
Test and debug a program with a range of test cases.
Work with a partner using pair programming, with a driver and a navigator.
Explain how numbers, text and images are represented in binary.
Collect data in a spreadsheet and display it in a chart.
Use data to find a pattern and draw a conclusion, and note what the data cannot show.
Describe how information is sent across the internet in packets.
Explain the roles of IP addresses, DNS and protocols.
Describe basic cybersecurity practices, including strong passwords and two-factor authentication.
Describe a computing innovation and its benefits and harms for different groups.
Explain issues of privacy and the digital footprint.
Create a small project that solves a problem for a real user and present it.
